arxiv-1604-06783.title: PyPanda: a Python Package for Gene Regulatory Network Reconstruction
arxiv-1604-06783.creator: David G.P. van IJzendoorn, Kimberly Glass, John Quackenbush, Marieke L. Kuijjer
arxiv-1604-06783.description: Abstract Summary : PANDA ( P assing A ttributes between N etworks for D ata A ssimilation) is a gene regulatory network inference method that uses message-passing to integrate multiple sources of ‘omics data. PANDA was originally coded in C++. In this application note we describe PyPanda, the Python version of PANDA.

arxiv-2101-08175.title: Bayesian GARCH Modeling of Functional Sports Data
arxiv-2101-08175.creator: Patric Dolmeta, Raffaele Argiento, Silvia Montagna
arxiv-2101-08175.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Patric Dolmeta, Raffaele Argiento, Silvia Montagna. The use of statistical methods in sport analytics has gained a rapidly growing interest over the last decade, and nowadays is common practice. In particular, the interest in understanding and predicting an athlete’s performance throughout his/her career is motivated by the need to evaluate the efficacy of training programs, anticipate fatigue to prevent injuries and detect unexpected of disproportionate increases in performance that might be indicative of doping.

arxiv-2104-14063.title: Nonuniform Berry-Esseen bound for self-normalized martingales Journal: the Académie des sciences
arxiv-2104-14063.creator: Songqi Wu, Lingjie Kong
arxiv-2104-14063.description: Abstract We give a nonuniform Berry-Esseen bound for self-normalized martingales, which bridges the gap between the results of Haeusler (1988) and Fan and Shao (2018). The bound coincides with the nonuniform Berry-Esseen bound of Haeusler and Joos (1988) for standardized martingales. As a consequence, a Berry-Esseen bound is obtained. 1 Introduction Let (X_{i},\mathcal{F}_{i})_{i=0,...

arxiv-2105-03710.title: Falling Through the Gaps: Neural Architectures as Models of Morphological Rule Learning
arxiv-2105-03710.creator: Deniz Beser (beser@isi.edu)
arxiv-2105-03710.description: Abstract Recent advances in neural architectures have revived the problem of morphological rule learning. We evaluate the Transformer as a model of morphological rule learning and compare it with Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) on English, German, and Russian. We bring to the fore a hitherto overlooked problem, the morphological gaps, where the expected inflection of a word is missing.

arxiv-2202-06119.title: Remarks on the L p L^{p} convergence of Bessel–Fourier series on the disc
arxiv-2202-06119.creator: Ryan L. Acosta Babb
arxiv-2202-06119.description: Abstract The L p L^{p} convergence of eigenfunction expansions for the Laplacian on planar domains is largely unknown for p ≠ 2 p\neq 2 . After discussing the classical Fourier series on the 2-torus, we move onto the disc, whose eigenfunctions are explicitly computable as products of trigonometric and Bessel functions.

arxiv-2302-07522.title: School of Particles and Accelerators,
arxiv-2302-07522.description: Abstract Three dimensional wormholes are global solutions of Einstein-Hilbert action. These space-times which are quotients of a part of global AdS 3 have multiple asymptotic regions, each with conformal boundary S 1 × ℝ S^{1}\times\mathbb{R} , and separated from each other by horizons.

arxiv-2308-02170.title: Sommerfeld enhancement for puffy self-interacting dark matter
arxiv-2308-02170.creator: Wenyu Wang, Wu-Long Xu, Jin Min Yang, Bin Zhu, Rui Zhu
arxiv-2308-02170.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Wenyu Wang, Wu-Long Xu, Jin Min Yang, Bin Zhu, Rui Zhu. We examine the Sommerfeld enhancement effect for the puffy self-interacting dark matter. We find out two new parameters to classify the self-scattering cross section into the Born, the resonance and the classical regimes for the puffy dark matter. Then we observe that the resonance peaks for the puffy dark matter self-scattering and for the Sommerfeld enhancement effect have the same locations.

arxiv-2310-13971.title: A well-balanced second-order finite volume approximation for a coupled system of granular flow
arxiv-2310-13971.creator: Aekta Aggarwal, Veerappa Gowda G. D, Sudarshan Kumar K
arxiv-2310-13971.description: Abstract A well-balanced second-order finite volume scheme is proposed and analyzed for a 2 × 2 2\times 2 system of non-linear partial differential equations which describes the dynamics of growing sandpiles created by a vertical source on a flat, bounded rectangular table in multiple dimensions.

arxiv-2401-09065.title: A unified scheme for calculating the exclusive semi-leptonic decays of hadrons
arxiv-2401-09065.creator: Guo-He Yang
arxiv-2401-09065.description: Abstract Exclusive semi-leptonic decay stands as a pivotal channel in the exploration of heavy flavor physics, primarily due to its straightforward experimental measurability. In this work, we delve into the hadron matrix element and hadron tensor within the context of exclusive semi-leptonic decays.

arxiv-2403-17529.title: Detection of Deepfake Environmental Audio
arxiv-2403-17529.creator: Hafsa Ouajdi, Oussama Hadder, Modan Tailleur, Mathieu Lagrange, Laurie M. Heller
arxiv-2403-17529.description: Abstract With the ever-rising quality of deep generative models, it is increasingly important to be able to discern whether the audio data at hand have been recorded or synthesized. Although the detection of fake speech signals has been studied extensively, this is not the case for the detection of fake environmental audio.

arxiv-2408-16176.title: VLM4Bio: A Benchmark Dataset to Evaluate Pretrained Vision-Language Models for Trait Discovery from Biological Images
arxiv-2408-16176.creator: M. Maruf, Arka Daw, Kazi Sajeed Mehrab, Harish Babu Manogaran, Abhilash Neog, Medha Sawhney, Mridul Khurana, James P. Balhoff, Yasin Bakış, Bahadir Altintas, Matthew J Thompson, Elizabeth G Campolongo, Josef C. Uyeda, Hilmar Lapp, Henry L. Bart Jr, Paula M. Mabee, Yu Su, Wei-Lun Chao, Charles Stewar
arxiv-2408-16176.description: Abstract Images are increasingly becoming the currency for documenting biodiversity on the planet, providing novel opportunities for accelerating scientific discoveries in the field of organismal biology, especially with the advent of large vision-language models (VLMs). We ask if pre-trained VLMs can aid scientists in answering a range of biologically relevant questions without any additional fine-tuning.

arxiv-2504-07038.title: Structured extensions and multi-correlation sequences
arxiv-2504-07038.creator: James Leng
arxiv-2504-07038.description: Abstract . We show that every multi-correlation sequence is the sum of a generalized nilsequence and a null-sequence. This proves a conjecture of N. Frantzikinakis. A key ingredient is the reduction of ergodic multidimensional inverse theorems to analogous finitary inverse theorems, offering a new approach to the structure theory of multidimensional Host-Kra factors.

arxiv-2505-22706.title: Variability in the massive black hole binary candidate SDSS J2320+0024: no evidence for periodic modulation
arxiv-2505-22706.creator: Fabio Rigamonti ,, Lorenzo Bertassi, Riccardo Buscicchio, Fabiola Cocchiararo, Stefano Covino, Massimo Dotti, Alberto Sesana, and Paola Severgnini
arxiv-2505-22706.description: Abstract Massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) are a natural outcome of galaxy mergers, and they are expected to be among the loudest gravitational wave sources at low frequencies. SDSS J2320+0024 has been recently proposed as a promising MBHB candidate due to a possible periodicity in its light-curve and variability in the MgII emission line.

arxiv-2508-06381.title: On the estimation of solar wind velocity under varying solar activity conditions using Akatsuki measurements 2026 On the estimation of solar wind velocity under varying solar activity conditions using Akatsuki measurements - References
arxiv-2508-06381.creator: Keshav Aggarwal, R. K. Choudhary, Abhirup Datta, T. Imamura
arxiv-2508-06381.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Keshav Aggarwal, R. K. Choudhary, Abhirup Datta, T. Imamura. We present an analysis of solar wind dynamics based on Doppler spectral width measurements of X-band radio signals from the Japanese Akatsuki spacecraft. The dataset includes two solar conjunction occultation experiments conducted in 2016 and 2022, capturing the transition from the descending phase of Solar Cycle 24, a period of low solar activity, to the ascending phase of Solar Cycle 25, which exhibited moderate to intense activity.

europmc-pmc9757867.creator: Bytyçi I, Penson PE, Mikhailidis DP, Wong ND, Hernandez AV, Sahebkar A, Thompson PD, Mazidi M, Rysz J, Pella D, Reiner Ž, Toth PP, Banach M.

Statin intolerance remains an important clinical challenge, and it is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular events. This meta-analysis

pmc-10480412.creator: Yuki Hayakawa, Kei Yamasaki, Midori Funada, Masaya Komatsu, Yukinori Maeda, Kazuhiro Yatera
pmc-10480412.description:

pmc-11458232.title: Brodie’s Abscess of the Ankle Presenting as a Tumor: A Summary of Five Cases
pmc-11458232.creator: Christopher Warburton, H Thomas Temple
pmc-11458232.description: Introduction:A Brodie’s abscess is a form of subacute osteomyelitis that is often considered in the differential diagnosis of other benign and malignant bone lesions. The authors summarize the findings of five cases of Brodie’s abscesses in the distal tibia initially thought to be tumors by the referring physicians.

pmc-11461823.creator: Ann-Kathrin Lederer, Kristina Endres

pmc-11570949.title: Effects of genotype and sex on carcass composition, meat quality, digestive tract morphometries and leg bone dimensions of spent parent Pekin ducks☆
pmc-11570949.creator: Marcin Wegner, Dariusz Kokoszyński, Joanna Żochowska-Kujawska, Marek Kotowicz
pmc-11570949.description: The purpose of the present study was to analyze carcass composition, physicochemical properties, muscle texture, and structure, as well as morphometry of the digestive tract and leg bone dimensions of Cherry Valley ducks (SM3 Heavy hybrid) and Orvia ducks (ST5 Heavy hybrid) after laying. A total of 32 ducks were dissected, 8 females and 8 males from each breeding set.

pmc-11633376.title: Cryo-EM structure of the Mycobacterium smegmatis MmpL5-AcpM complex
pmc-11633376.creator: Rakesh Maharjan, Zhemin Zhang, Philip A. Klenotic, William D. Gregor, Georgiana E. Purdy, Edward W. Yu
pmc-11633376.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the causative agent of the airborne infection tuberculosis (TB), contains 13 mycobacterial membrane protein large (MmpL) transporters that can be divided into two distinct subclasses. These MmpL proteins play important functional roles within the mycobacterium and subsequently are considered attractive drug targets to combat TB infection.

pmc-11664729.title: Evaluation of Error Sources for an Image-Based Computer Assisted Surgical System for Total Ankle Arthroplasty
pmc-11664729.creator: Matthew C Rueff, Zach Tupper, Matthew Hamilton, Prudhvi Chinimilli, Scott Gulbransen, Laureline Prouvost, Edward T Haupt, Laurent Angibaud, Dipl Ing
pmc-11664729.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Category:Ankle; Ankle ArthritisIntroduction/Purpose:Computer Assisted Surgical (CAS) systems have been used successfully in joint arthroplasty to improve the accuracy of bony resections. CAS usage leads to reduced outliers and improved targeted alignment of orthopedic implants.

pmc-11676869.title: Promoter of Vegetable Pea PsPIP2-4 Responds to Abiotic Stresses in Transgenic Tobacco
pmc-11676869.creator: Zhijuan Feng, Na Liu, Yuanpeng Bu, Guwen Zhang, Bin Wang, Yaming Gong, Pedro Martínez-Gómez
pmc-11676869.description: Plasma membrane intrinsic proteins (PIPs), one sub-family of aquaporins (AQPs), are responsible for plant abiotic stress responses. However, little information is currently available about the stress responsiveness of the PIP promoter in vegetable pea. In the present study, one novel promoter of PsPIP2-4 which shared high similarity to the PIP2-type AQPs from other plants, was isolated.

pmc-12522659.title: Relationship between stroke injury sites and incidence of post-stroke pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12522659.creator: Zhifa Zhang, Sehui Ma, Bin Feng, Xiaoying Li, Yufen Zhang, Lei Pei
pmc-12522659.description: BackgroundPost-stroke pain (PSP) is a prevalent and debilitating complication of stroke recovery, mainly characterized by allodynia and hyperalgesia. While certain brain lesion sites, particularly thalamic lesions, have been implicated in an increased risk of PSP, evidence regarding the specific contributions of stroke injury sites to PSP development remains inconsistent.

pmc-12595727.title: Tumor index predicts recurrences of patients with pathological stage Ⅰ gastric cancer after radical surgical resection
pmc-12595727.creator: Yijia Lin, Huaxian Chen, Chengzhi Wei, Dandong Luo, Jianping Guo, Xiansheng Hu, Yinghan Chen, Junsheng Peng, Yongming Chen, Lei Lian
pmc-12595727.description: BackgroundDespite the favorable prognosis of patients with pathological stage I gastric cancer (GC), recurrence may occur in a subset of individuals, and the underlying risk factors are currently being investigated. Tumor index (TI) plays a valuable role in predicting the prognosis of GC. The study aimed to determine the prognostic effect of TI on stage Ⅰ GC.

pmc-12776133.title: Combination of Naples prognostic score and pathological factors for evaluating the long-term prognosis of patients with late-onset colorectal cancer: a multicenter machine learning study
pmc-12776133.creator: Tawfik Ali Hamood Alburiahi, Yan-Hong Yang, Weiqing Liu, Xin Li, Wanrong Lin, Lei Liang, Jun Yang
pmc-12776133.description: BackgroundGiven the increasingly aging population, precise prognostic models are essential for optimizing postoperative care in patients with late-onset colorectal cancer (LOCRC). Inflammatory, immune, and nutritional factors, along with the Naples prognostic score (NPS), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and clinicopathological variables, are emerging as predictors of postoperative outcomes in patients with LOCRC.

pmc-13049148.title: A bio-polymeric strategy for enhancing the strength, durability of concrete and shrinkage reduction
pmc-13049148.creator: Kunamineni Vijay, V. V. S. Sarma, Venkateswarlu Kuruva, A. Uday Kumar, Kemal Detu, Panga Narasimha Reddy
pmc-13049148.description: The formation of cracks in concrete is inevitable and often accelerated by inadequate curing. In many regions, the availability of potable water for external curing is limited, leading to improper curing practices and the development of shrinkage cracks. Resolving this issue is essential to enhancing concrete structures’ long-term performance.

pmc-13487937.title: The intensive outreach programme for child and adolescent eating disorders: an uncontrolled case series of clinical characteristics and treatment outcomes
pmc-13487937.creator: Cliona Brennan, Ellen McAdams, Elena Pears, Paula Herrera-Gener, Julian Baudinet, Mima Simic
pmc-13487937.description: IntroductionDespite growing interest, empirical evidence remains limited for the efficacy of intensive outpatient programmes (IOPs) for eating disorders (EDs), particularly outside the USA. No prior studies have examined the delivery or effectiveness of IOPs for children and young people in the UK.
